extracted.intended_audience: applicants, recipients, and institutional grants administrators for NIH awards
extracted.subtask_short: NIH grant cost and admin policies
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards governing allowable costs, salary charging, travel, facilities, and administrative actions (carryover, prior approvals, extensions) for NIH grants and recipients. Covers documentation, special situations (sabbatical, consulting, dual appointments), and procedures for post-award changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research patient care costs exclusion (personal expenses)
rubrics_metrics.description: The following otherwise allowable costs are not classified as research patient care costs: items of personal expense such as patient travel; consulting physician fees; and any other direct payments to individuals, including inpatients, outpatients, subjects, volunteers, and donors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such costs should be included in the 'Other Expenses' category of the grant budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve funds for self-insurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributions to a reserve fund for self-insurance are allowable as specified in the governing cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See related sections (Fringe Benefits/Insurance and Contingency Provisions) for applicable limitations and treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Part-time faculty charges (IHEs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for work performed on Federal awards by faculty members having only part-time appointments will be determined at a rate not in excess of that regularly paid for part-time assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must reflect the institution's regular part-time pay practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charges outside academic year (IBS limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified for teaching activity, charges for work performed by faculty on Federal awards during periods not included in the base salary period will be at a rate not in excess of the institutional base salary (IBS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching activity during non-IBS periods has separate rules (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sabbatical leave costs and charging
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges for teaching activities performed during periods not in the IBS will be based on the IHE's normal written policy governing compensation for such teaching assignments. Sabbatical leave costs may be included in a fringe benefit rate or the indirect cost rate. Salary may be charged directly for services rendered while on sabbatical if proportional to service and paid according to established organizational policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sabbatical leave paid by employer combined with other compensation (e.g., partial NIH salary) may not exceed 100% of the individual's regular institutional salary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for documentation of personnel expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary and wage amounts charged to grant-supported projects must be based on an adequate payroll distribution system that documents such distribution in accordance with Federal Cost Principles and consistently applied institutional policy and practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 CFR Part 200.430(i) for documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of compensation for personal services
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation for personal services (including fringe benefits) is allowable to the extent it is reasonable, conforms to established institutional policy consistently applied regardless of funding source, and reasonably reflects the percentage of time actually devoted to the NIH-funded project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct salary is exclusive of fringe benefits and indirect costs; guidance does not apply to consultant payments or routine contracts (but applies to consortium participants). Salaries of federal employees with permanent appointments are generally unallowable except in specified circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extra service pay (overload) — allowability conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extra service pay is allowable if all of the following are met: (1) IHE has consistent written policies applying uniformly to all faculty; (2) IHE defines IBS specifically enough to determine when work beyond that level occurs; (3) supplementation is commensurate with IBS and extra work; (4) supplemented salaries fall within documented IHE pay ranges; (5) total salaries charged including extra service pay meet Standards of Documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extra service pay is subject to reasonableness standards and applies when work is above IBS; see examples of allowable activities contributing directly to award work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable activities for personnel compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Charges to Federal awards may include reasonable amounts for activities directly related to the work, such as delivering special lectures about the activity, writing reports and articles, developing/maintaining protocols, managing substances/chemicals and project-specific data, coordinating research subjects, participating in seminars, consulting with colleagues/graduate students, and attending meetings and conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intra-IHE consulting is assumed part of IHE obligation (no extra comp) except in unusual cross-departmental or remote cases, where additional compensation may be allowable if provided for in the award or approved in writing by the NIH awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charging consulting fees — organizational policy requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients, consortium participants, and contractors must establish written guidelines permitting payments of employee consulting costs regardless of funding source and indicating conditions under which consulting fees are proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under no circumstances may an individual be paid as both a consultant and an employee under the same NIH grant. Authorization for consulting fees when individuals are both employees and consultants must be documented in writing, case-by-case, by the head of the organization (or designee), and must include determination that conditions are present and no conflict of interest exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compensation to nonprofit organization leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation to members of nonprofit organizations (trustees, directors, officers, associates, and immediate families) should be determined to be reasonable for actual personal services rendered rather than a distribution of earnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May include director’s fees, incentive awards, off-site pay allowances, location differentials, hardship pay, and cost-of-living differentials, but must be justified as reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional activities outside recipient/subrecipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Where written policies do not adequately define permissible outside consulting or non-organizational activities, the Federal government may require allocation of effort between (1) recipient/subrecipient activities, and (2) non-organizational professional activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If NIH considers non-organizational effort excessive or inconsistent with conflicts-of-interest terms, compensation arrangements will be negotiated case-by-case with the awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations for changes in compensation policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Special consideration will be given to any change in a recipient's compensation policy resulting in a substantial increase in employees' compensation (particularly concurrent with an increase in ratio of Federal awards to other activities) or change due to Federal policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will scrutinize policy changes that may affect allowability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unallowable costs under personnel compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs unallowable under other sections of these principles are not made allowable solely because they are personnel compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must review all applicable sections for unallowable items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incentive compensation allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Incentive compensation based on cost reduction, efficient performance, suggestion awards, safety awards, etc., is allowable to the extent overall compensation is reasonable and such costs are paid pursuant to a good-faith agreement entered into before services were rendered or pursuant to an established consistent plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Must be determined reasonable in aggregate; documentation of plan or agreement required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overtime premiums
rubrics_metrics.description: Premiums for overtime are generally allowable; however, such payments are not allowable for faculty members at institutions of higher education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If overtime premiums are allowable, eligibility categories must be determined by formally established organizational policies consistently applied regardless of funding source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payments for dual appointments (clinical practice inclusion in IBS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical practice compensation may be included in the institutional base salary (IBS) and charged to NIH agreements if all of the following are met: (1) compensation set by the institution; (2) clinical practice activity shown on institution payroll/salary appointment forms approved by the institution; (3) compensation paid through or at the direction of the institution; (4) activity included and accounted for in effort reporting/payroll distribution; (5) institution assures financial reports and supporting documents for combined IBS and charges are retained and made available consistent with 2 CFR Part 200.430.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Set by the institution' requires documentation that the specified amount is paid in essentially the same manner as other committed IBS and that IBS does not vary based on specific clinical services provided during certified periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selling and marketing costs generally unallowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs of selling and marketing any products or services of the recipient or subrecipient are generally not allowable, except as direct costs with prior approval by the NIH awarding IC when necessary for performance of the Federal award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 2 CFR Part 200.421 for any allowed exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specialized service facilities charging rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs to a user of organizational services and central facilities (e.g., central lab, computing) are allowable provided they are not covered by indirect costs and are based on organizational fee schedules consistently applied regardless of funding source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When services are highly complex/specialized: (1) charges must meet conditions of paragraphs (b) or (c) (i.e., direct charging rules) and account for applicable credits; (2) when material, charge directly based on actual usage and an established rate methodology that does not discriminate and recovers only aggregate costs; (3) immaterial costs may be allocated as indirect; (4) extraordinary alternative costing arrangements may be negotiated with the Federal cognizant agency. Rates must be adjusted at least biennially and consider over/under applied costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stipends allowable only under NRSA training awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Stipends are allowable as cost-of-living allowances for trainees and fellows only under Kirschstein-NRSA individual fellowships and institutional research training grants and follow preestablished schedules based on experience and level of training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A stipend is not a fee-for-service and is not subject to cost accounting requirements of the cost principles. Stipends are not allowable under research grants even if they appear to benefit the research project; see NRSA stipend supplementation policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxes — allowability and exceptions for nonprofit organizations and IHEs
rubrics_metrics.description: In general, taxes required to be paid and paid or accrued in accordance with GAAP, and payments to local governments in lieu of taxes commensurate with services received, are allowable, except: (a) taxes from which exemptions are available to recipient/subrecipient directly or via Federal exemption certificates; (b) special assessments on land representing capital improvements; (c) Federal income taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any refund of taxes allowed as Federal award costs must be credited as a cost reduction or cash refund to the Federal government; interest paid or credited on refunds is payable/creditable to the Federal government to the extent interest accrued during the period the recipient was reimbursed by the Federal government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination or suspension costs (allowability)
rubrics_metrics.description: Termination of a Federal award may lead to additional costs; cost principles covering termination costs are set forth in 2 CFR 200.472 and must be used with termination requirements in Section 8.5.2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients may not incur new obligations after effective date of suspension/termination that are not directly associated with termination; NIH will allow full credit for Federal share of otherwise allowable costs if obligations were properly incurred before suspension/termination, not in anticipation of it, and in case of termination are not cancelable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trailers and modular units — real property vs equipment classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A trailer or modular unit is considered real property when unit and installation are designed/planned to be installed permanently and appear fixed to land; considered equipment when intended for limited-time use. Allowability depends on classification: real property not chargeable unless legislation permits and NIH approval; equipment may be charged only if award terms permit and NIH prior approval obtained as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification at acquisition remains for the life of the item and determines accountability requirements under 2 CFR Part 200.439 or 200.465.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transportation costs allowability
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs for freight, express, cartage, postage, and other transportation services relating to goods purchased, in process, or delivered are allowable. When readily identifiable with items, charge directly; otherwise inbound transportation may be charged to indirect cost accounts if consistent equitable procedure followed. Outbound freight, if reimbursable, should be direct charged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow consistent institutional procedures for allocation between direct and indirect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel costs — allowability and policy compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel is allowable as a direct cost where it provides direct benefit to the project and must be consistent with the organization's travel policy. For air travel, the lowest reasonable commercial airfares must be used. For-profit recipients' travel costs may not exceed FTR limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no institutional travel policy exists, FTR regulations will be used. Recipients are encouraged to use discount fares via advance purchase. Recipients must comply with Fly America Act for foreign air travel funded by Federal funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research patient travel and vehicle costs
rubrics_metrics.description: If research patient care is an approved activity, costs of transporting individuals participating in the research protocol to the service site (including public transportation) are allowable, and purchase of motor vehicles for this purpose also may be allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Research Patient Care section for further details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign taxes and value added tax (VAT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign taxes legally required to be paid for purchase of goods or services are allowable under Federal awards. Foreign tax refunds or applicable credits that offset costs allocable to Federal awards must be credited to the NIH awarding IC either as costs or cash refunds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If credits relate to allowable costs, recipients may reduce Federal share or, with prior NIH approval, use foreign tax refund for approved activities under the award. Many countries exempt research from such taxes, making request for the cost unallowable in those cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visa costs — recruiting vs renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: Visa costs (including short-term travel visa costs) are generally allowable as direct recruiting costs if the institution has an employer/employee relationship with the individual, or when identified in NOFOs or within scope of an approved research project. Visa renewal costs for employees are not recruiting costs and are not allowable. Expedited processing fees are generally unallowable unless they become standard processing fees. Fraud prevention/detection fees and required DHS SEVIS Form I-901 fees are allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish recruiting-related visa costs (allowable) from renewal/employee visa maintenance (not allowable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of significant developments
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to notify NIH of developments that have a significant impact on award-supported activities as soon as they become known, including significant changes to Other Support (e.g., new appointments/affiliations) and problems, delays, or adverse conditions materially impairing ability to meet award objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification should include actions taken or contemplated and any assistance needed to resolve the situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient authorities and expanded authorities (standard terms of award)
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH recipients have certain authorities to rebudget and make post-award changes without prior approval (expanded authorities), but some authorities are excluded (e.g., automatic carryover of unobligated balances for centers, cooperative agreements, certain training and SBIR/STTR awards, clinical trials, awards to individuals). Individual awards may further restrict authority via NoA terms and conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must review the Notice of Award (NoA) to determine if specific authorities are withheld; exercise proper stewardship and ensure costs are allowable, allocable, reasonable, necessary, and consistently applied—NIH may disallow costs failing these tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carryover of unobligated balances — automatic authority and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Automatic carryover of unobligated balances applies to all awards except centers (P50, P60, P30, others), cooperative agreements (U), Kirschstein-NRSA institutional training grants (T), non-Fast Track Phase I SBIR/STTR (R43/R41), clinical trials, and awards to individuals (unless NoA indicates otherwise). For excluded awards carryover requires NIH awarding IC prior approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SNAP awards, funds are automatically carried over but the recipient must indicate in progress report if estimated unobligated balance is expected to be greater than 25% of current year's total approved budget and provide explanation/plans for expenditure. For both SNAP and non-SNAP, GMO will review balances >25% and may request revised budget or take actions (restrict authority, reduce funding, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and time limits for carryover and account closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: All Federal agencies must close fixed year appropriation accounts and cancel remaining balances by September 30 of the fifth fiscal year after year of availability. Recipients must report disbursements on the FFR no later than August 31 of the fifth fiscal year after year of availability to avoid cancellation of funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may limit carryover availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unliquidated obligations vs unobligated balances
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients should distinguish unliquidated obligations (commitments considered obligations and not reported as unobligated balances) from unobligated balances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NoA will include terms indicating disposition of unobligated balances and whether automatic carryover authority applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-related prior approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH prior approval is not required to rebudget funds for any direct cost item that the applicable cost principles identify as requiring prior approval, unless the incurrence of costs is associated with or considered a change in scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must determine whether a rebudget constitutes a change in scope; if so, prior approval is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-time no-cost extension (final budget period extension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipient may extend the final budget period of a previously approved project period one time for up to 12 months beyond original completion date if: (1) no term of award specifically prohibits the extension; (2) no additional funds are required; (3) the project's originally approved scope will not change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension must reflect that additional work remains or orderly closeout is needed; remaining funds alone are not sufficient justification. Some grant programs with effort requirements or specific terms may prohibit reductions in effort without prior approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction in effort for Senior/Key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for grant programs that have an effort requirement or where terms prohibit such reductions, NIH will not require prior approval for reduction in effort for Senior/Key personnel named in the NoA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are reminded that active awards must have a measurable level of effort.
